questions.prompt: Which PROUD value focuses on including others?
Which British Value says breaches 'may have disciplinary or legal consequences'?
questions.explanation: Rule of Law - breaches may have disciplinary or legal consequences.

questions.prompt: Which of these are protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Race, religion or belief, and sexual orientation are three of the nine protected characteristics. Being a student rep is not.

questions.prompt: How does the deck define victimisation under the Equality Act?
options: Treating someone less favourably because of a protected characteristic
Treating someone unfairly because they raised - or supported - a discrimination concern
Repeated behaviour intended to intimidate, control, or harm
questions.explanation: Victimisation is treating someone unfairly because they raised - or supported - a discrimination concern.

questions.prompt: On placement, who should you report concerns to, according to the deck?
options: No one - it's not your job
Your teacher - not just the placement provider
questions.explanation: Report concerns to your teacher, not just the placement provider.

questions.prompt: What's the deck's view of content posted outside college?
options: It can't affect you at college
It can still lead to disciplinary action
Only if it's posted during term time
Only if it's tagged with the college
questions.explanation: Content posted outside college can still lead to disciplinary action.

questions.prompt: Which of these are routes for reporting a concern, according to the deck? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Tell your teacher, formal reporting system, and anonymous reporting are the three routes.
